conventions.convention: Rademacher indices start at j=0. Integrals are over [0,1) with restricted Borel Lebesgue measure; binary digits use floor, fixing dyadic-endpoint values.
The dyadic partition is inhomogeneous: φ0=ψ, φj=ψ(2⁻ʲ·)−ψ(2⁻⁽ʲ⁻¹⁾·) for j≥1, and φ−1=0. Companion symbols sum the three neighbouring pieces. The low block and its companion have kernel integral 1.
SN sums j=0,…,N−1; S is the increasing pointwise limit of continuous convolution representatives, initially allowed to be infinite. The norm equivalence is restricted to 1<p<∞.

Hs uses the exact Japanese-bracket weight (1+|ξ|²)ˢ⸍² and the canonical completion embedding into tempered distributions; this is distinct from the Laplacian weight (1+4π²|ξ|²)ˢ⸍². The dyadic low-block weight is 1.
Kruzhkov solutions are space–time almost-everywhere classes. sgn(0)=0. The initial trace is the essential supremum over sufficiently small positive times of the local L1 discrepancy.

Shock jumps are plus minus minus; the space–time normal points from the minus side toward the plus side. For x=s(t), the normal is (−s′,1)/√(1+s′²). Entropy production has coefficient [q]−s′[η] and must be nonpositive.

The local contraction estimate is for each fixed centre and radius and almost every time with Lt<R; its exceptional set may depend on that ball. Every-time conclusions use a chosen local-L1-continuous representative.
Vanishing-viscosity compactness uses Dependent Choice, which supplies the required Countable Choice. The existence, Oleinik, Hamilton–Jacobi, and semigroup consumers retain these assumptions.
The Hamilton–Jacobi primitive is normalized as U(t,x)=∫₋∞ˣu(t,y)dy−tf(0). The two correspondence classes are bounded Lipschitz initial potentials and compactly supported L1∩L∞ initial derivatives.
For Λ=Aℤn, covolume is |det A| and Λ*=A⁻ᵀℤn. Characters use exp(2πiξ·x); Fourier transformation uses exp(−2πix·ξ).
The lattice fundamental cell is A((0,1]n); its translates partition Euclidean space exactly, rather than merely modulo null boundaries.

Sampling uses h>0, the centered band [−1/(2h),1/(2h)], the continuous inverse-transform representative, and sinc(t)=sin(πt)/(πt), with sinc(0)=1. The rescaled spectrum is reflected to match negative-sign Fourier coefficients.
Nyquist disjointness is modulo null sets. The distributional sampling formula remains Schwartz-only; Shannon's stated pointwise clause assumes absolutely summable samples.

load_bearing.statement: Assume Countable Choice. For a C1 flux that is L-Lipschitz on [−M,M] and bounded Kruzhkov solutions u,v with |u|,|v|≤M, each fixed x0,R>0 satisfies ∫B(x0,R−Lt)|u(t)−v(t)|≤∫B(x0,R)|u0−v0| for almost every t∈(0,T) with Lt<R. The exceptional set may depend on x0,R.

Assume Countable Choice and Dependent Choice. For n≥1, T>0, a locally Lipschitz C1 flux f, and u0∈L∞∩L1, there exists a unique bounded Kruzhkov solution with a representative in C([0,T];L1loc), strong local L1 initial trace u0, and ‖u(t)‖∞≤‖u0‖∞ at every time.

Assume Countable Choice. For ε>0, a C2 flux f with f(0)=0, and u0∈Cc∞, compatible global mild solutions exist in C([0,T];Cb)∩C([0,T];L1)∩C1,2 at positive times, solve ut+div f(u)=εΔu, and remain between the initial infimum and supremum. No uniqueness beyond the constructed mild solution is asserted.

Assume Dependent Choice. For fixed smooth compact datum u0, C2 normalized fluxes fj with uniformly bounded derivatives on [−‖u0‖∞−1,‖u0‖∞+1], and εj↓0 in (0,1], every subsequence of the viscous solutions has a further subsequence converging locally in space–time L1, and then almost everywhere, to a bounded limit with a C([0,T];L1loc) representative and initial value u0.

Assume Countable Choice. For the fixed inhomogeneous partition and every 1<p<∞, cp‖f‖p≤‖Sf‖p≤Cp‖f‖p on Schwartz space and Lp. Schwartz approximation gives the unique continuous extension, identified almost everywhere with the increasing convolution square function; SNf converges to Sf in Lp and almost everywhere.

For any radial smooth compact cutoff 0≤ψ≤1 equal to 1 on the unit ball and supported inside the radius-two ball, φ0=ψ and φj=ψ(2⁻ʲ·)−ψ(2⁻⁽ʲ⁻¹⁾·) form a locally finite partition of unity, with the stated annular supports, nonnegative pieces, at most three nonzero pieces, 1/3≤Σφj²≤1, and uniform scaled derivative bounds. Such a cutoff exists, vanishing at radius 3/2.

Assume Countable Choice. For every finite complex coefficient family indexed by nonnegative integers and every 0<p<∞, the Lp norm on [0,1) of its Rademacher sum is comparable to its Euclidean coefficient norm, with constants depending only on p. At p=2 the equality is exact; empty sums are zero.

Assume Countable Choice. For every tempered distribution f, Σj<N companion-Δj Δj f converges to f in tempered distributions. For Schwartz f,g the finite Hermitian pairing identity holds; if Sf∈Lp and companion-Sg∈Lp′, the pairing series converges absolutely to ⟨f,g⟩ and is bounded by ∫Sf companion-Sg.

For a one-dimensional C1 flux and a single nontrivial piecewise C1 weak jump satisfying Rankine–Hugoniot, all convex entropy inequalities hold iff F(z)(u+−u−)≥0 between the states, where F(z)=f(z)−f(u−)−s′(z−u−). Increasing jumps require the graph above the chord; decreasing jumps require it below.

Assume Countable Choice. For Schwartz f and a full-rank lattice Λ of covolume c and dual Λ*, both lattice sums converge absolutely and ΣΛf(λ)=c⁻¹ΣΛ*f̂(λ*). More precisely, ΣΛf(x+λ)=c⁻¹ΣΛ*f̂(λ*)exp(2πiλ*·x) for every x.

Assume Countable Choice. If h>0 and f∈L2 has Plancherel spectrum supported almost everywhere in [−1/(2h),1/(2h)], it has a continuous inverse-integral representative. The periodic spectrum Gh(θ)=h⁻¹⸍²f̂(−θ/h) has coefficients h¹⸍²f(hk), and Σk|f(hk)|²=h⁻¹‖f‖2².

Assume Countable Choice. For h>0 and an L2 signal supported spectrally in the centered band [−1/(2h),1/(2h)], its continuous representative satisfies f=Σkf(hk)sinc(·/h−k) in L2. If Σk|f(hk)|<∞, the series converges absolutely and uniformly on compact sets and equals f at every point.
